summary.headline: MedPlus Q4 FY26: consolidated revenue INR18,644 mn and operating EBITDA margin 5.8%; FY27 plan of 800 net new stores, including franchisees.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net store additions were 218 (295 openings, 77 closures) taking the network to 5,330 stores, with 618 net additions over FY26. Consolidated revenue was INR18,644 mn and operating EBITDA INR1,076 mn (5.8%), with pharmacy revenue up 23.4% YoY on a reported basis. Stores older than 12 months delivered a 13.1% store-level EBITDA margin and 96% of pharmacy revenue. Management introduced a franchisee model (about 310 franchisee stores added in FY26, 500-plus in total) and a corrigendum raised FY26 operating cash flow to INR4,956 mn.

segments.name: Pharmacy (company-owned stores)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating EBITDA INR1,022 million (5.6%) on pharmacy revenue up 23.4% YoY; 24% of stores are under 2 years old and 76% are 2 years or older.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR347.8 million (up from INR280.8 million) with 15.3% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue INR1,309.9 million and operating EBITDA INR196 million. Active plans about 2 lakh at 31 March; on-time renewal rate 21% in Q4 vs 23% in Q3.

segments.name: Franchisee model (new)
segments.commentary: Company capex about INR10 lakh per store; franchisee buys inventory outright on day one. Pharmacy gross margin 24% is split roughly 14-14.5% to franchisee and 9.5-10% to MedPlus, before supply-chain cost of about 2.5-3%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 plan: 800 net new stores including franchisee outlets; no split between company-owned and franchisee provided.
Management aims to sustain operating EBITDA margin of 5.7-5.8% over the next year before growing it further; no formal guidance given.
Gross margin expected to at least be maintained; further private label gains expected to be accretive.
Mature-store SSSG target of 9-10% annually reiterated.
Private label guidance intact: 20-30 bps quarterly increase in share, with every 0.3% gain in private label adding 0.1% to gross margin.
Warehouse inventory expected to stay in the 30-33 day range; tail-brand reduction considered only once MedPlus brand reaches 40%-plus share.
Dividend not yet considered; management will discuss with senior management and Board.
capex_capacity: Plan to upgrade or modernise 600-plus stores this year to add more assortment, including rack-system changes and pharma/non-pharma demarcation.
New warehouses needed for newer states; the 800-store plan within existing states needs only a few warehouses, far fewer than the current year's additions.
Own manufacturing in place for bakery products, cleaning liquids and toiletries; contract manufacturers used where capacity is lacking.
Diagnostics: plans sold at 537 gross per day in January, 603 in February and 554 in March.
demand_pricing: Q4 mature-store SSSG reported at a strong level (analyst cited 17.8%, strongest in about 12-13 quarters); management attributed it to full assortment availability and FMCG uptick, not a special initiative.
Private label non-pharma gross margin 23-25% vs 9-10% for branded non-pharma; private label pharma commands higher margin still.
Store closures in Q4 include 26-27 mature stores (three years or older) closed on underperformance, 18 relocations and 13 franchisee outlets.
Q4 gross margin up 30 bps QoQ, helped by higher other income, pharma membership income and supplier incentives accrued on units sold.
Online is 5-plus% of total sales; GLP-1 impact not tracked, cold chain infrastructure already in place from injectables and vaccines.
Pharma returns to suppliers are limited to expiries, under 1% of sales, with up to 95% reimbursed within about a month.

qa_highlights.question: Why are store closures rising, and why are franchisee withdrawals up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 26-27 stores aged three years or more were closed for underperformance; other closures are explained in the investor deck, and early franchisee exits are normal within the first two months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the private label growth guidance of 20-30 bps per quarter still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said the trajectory is back on track after restructuring incentives in the last two quarters, but gave no specific growth number.

qa_highlights.question: How is the franchisee model's capex, inventory and margin structured?
qa_highlights.answer: MedPlus funds about INR10 lakh per store capex; franchisees buy inventory outright from day one; MedPlus keeps about 9.5-10% gross margin on the franchise sale, with supply-chain cost of 2.5-3% charged separately and no marketing fee charged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 12-month-plus store margin of 6.7% up from 5.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed there was no one-off; the increase came from operating performance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend stance given free cash flow after lease payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has not yet reached that stage, has huge headroom to invest, and will take the question to the senior management and Board.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost of INR120 crore on a supposed INR1,600 crore loan?
qa_highlights.answer: The interest relates entirely to lease accounting under Ind AS; the company has no external borrowings and is described as zero-debt.

risks_watch: Rising store closures (Q4 net addition 218 vs 182 in Q3) and franchisee exits; watch whether the closure trend persists.
Franchisee model economics: gross margin on franchise sales is about 9.5-10% versus about 24% company-level, and the supply-chain cost has not been disclosed in full.
Diagnostics renewal rate fell to 21% in Q4 from 23% in Q3.
Private label gross margin dilution risk if non-pharma and franchisee mix grows faster than private label share.
Inventory risk: private label expiry and write-off sits fully on MedPlus' books; first-year store inventory is 112 days.
Store space constraints for adding private label non-pharma range; 600-plus store upgrade project to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the franchisee model, but guarded on numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance beyond maintaining the current 5.7-5.8% EBITDA margin and 9-10% SSSG. It was evasive on the franchisee store split, GLP-1 impact, franchisee revenue and dividend policy, deferring these to later.
key_quotes: Yeah, as a principle, the company does not give guidance, but there is no reason to believe that we will not continue in the same manner.
On the private label, the entire inventory risk of expiry and write-off is on our books.
So we have not taken that call yet, but I'll take your question back and discuss with the senior management and the Board.

growth.why: Management plans 800 net new stores in FY27 (including franchisees, no split given) and reiterates 9-10% mature-store SSSG and 5.7-5.8% EBITDA margin; store count is specific but no revenue growth number is guided, and Q4 pharmacy revenue grew 23.4% YoY on a reported basis.
